fine_lines.title: raw vs cooked
fine_lines.explanation_ar: raw = نيّء لم يُطبخ. cooked = مطبوخ.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Raw" = not cooked. "Cooked" = made hot and ready.

examples.sentence: The rice must be cooked first.

fine_lines.title: slice vs chop
fine_lines.explanation_ar: slice = تقطيع إلى شرائح رقيقة مسطحة. chop = تقطيع إلى قطع صغيرة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Slice" = cut into thin flat pieces. "Chop" = cut into small pieces.

examples.sentence: Chop the onion into small pieces.

expressions.meaning_en: Asking if something is a problem (often a joke).
expressions.example: A surprise? Should I be worried?
Cooking with friends? This could be interesting.

expressions.meaning_en: You are doing a lot of work for it.
expressions.example: You cooked five dishes? You're really going all out!
You cook and I wash the dishes. Deal.
Do you need any help with the cooking?
Cook the rice and let it cool? Sounds easy enough.

expressions.phrase: It turned out better than I expected.
expressions.example: The cake turned out better than I expected.

expressions.meaning_en: The hard work was good because the result is good.
expressions.example: The long trip was worth the effort.

grammar.title: Present perfect with never
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم have/has + never + التصريف الثالث لنقول إننا لم نفعل شيئًا أبدًا حتى الآن.
grammar.explanation_en: Use have/has + never + past participle for something you have not done in your life until now.
examples: She has never used a rice cooker.

grammar.title: Instructions: imperatives and "We just need to ..."
grammar.explanation_ar: في الوصفات نستخدم صيغة الأمر (Cook, Slice, Add) أو We just need to + الفعل.
grammar.explanation_en: Recipes use imperatives (Cook, Slice, Add) or "We just need to + verb".
examples: Cook the rice and let it cool.
Slice the fish into thin pieces.
We just need to arrange it on top of the rice.
